clue.text: Fourth point-accommodation

parts.note: a fourth part of anything is a quarter
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A clue that reads like a geometry instruction about a fourth point being fitted in.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarters are lodgings, the rooms where soldiers or staff are housed.

clue.text: Full (unlimited) time comes round at last

indicators.note: without its limits, the word Full loses its first and last letters
the word for time is put around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football match running to full time, with the final whistle coming round at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full' looks like the definition but gives only its inner letters; 'last' at the end is the definition. 'unlimited' and 'comes round' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means final, coming at the very end of a series.

clue.text: His story was based on one long lie

definitions.text: His story was based on one long lie

parts.words: His story was based on one long lie
parts.note: the lie is not a falsehood but a lie-down: the hero of Washington Irving's tale slept for twenty years

explanation.surface: A liar whose whole account rests on a single sustained deception.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irving's story the character sleeps in the Catskills for twenty years, one very long lie-down.

clue.text: Where possibility of skin-grafting is in question

definitions.text: Where possibility of skin-grafting is in question

parts.words: Where possibility of skin-grafting is in question
parts.note: alludes to Jeremiah's question 'Can the ... change his skin?', so this is the country where changing skin is doubted

explanation.surface: A medical query about where skin grafts might be possible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible (Jeremiah 13:23) asks whether a man of this land can change his skin, implying he cannot.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical proverb about an African nation's people changing skin makes it the place where that is questioned.

clue.text: Reel answer to the holidays problem

definitions.meaning: to reel is to totter or lurch unsteadily
employers spread out staff leave so not everyone is away at once

explanation.definitionFit: To lurch is to totter; and spreading leave dates across a workforce avoids everyone being away together.

clue.text: Practice run for fish about close of day

indicators.note: the fish's name goes about, enclosing, the other letter

parts.note: a trout is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from day

explanation.surface: An angler's practice outing for fish at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial or test, such as a sports team's audition session.

clue.text: Polish up the interior of the grain-store

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read bottom to top
the inside letters of Polish are taken, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone told to polish up the inside of a grain store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the interior of' takes OLIS from Polish; 'up' turns it to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tower used for storing grain on a farm.

clue.text: Press with its troubles goes stubbornly on

indicators.note: the letters are troubled, stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper with its problems doggedly keeps printing.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly despite opposition.

clue.text: " He taught us " the Mock Turtle explained

definitions.text: " He taught us " the Mock Turtle explained

parts.words: " He taught us " the Mock Turtle explained
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Mock Turtle says the old master was called this because he taught us, a pun on the sound

explanation.surface: A quotation from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland about a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's Mock Turtle: 'We called him Tortoise because he taught us.'
explanation.definitionFit: The slow shelled reptile's name is said like the phrase about teaching, Carroll's joke.

clue.text: No go period

definitions.meaning: a halt, the signal not to proceed
the full point that ends a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: A halt means no going on; a full point closes a sentence.

clue.text: Like Captain Bobadil I long for change in different surroundings

indicators.note: the word for different forms surroundings around the other piece

parts.note: various means diverse, different

indicators.note: the letters of the words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A braggart soldier yearning for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' is the anagram signal and 'surroundings' the container. Captain Bobadil is the boastful soldier in Ben Jonson's play Every Man in His Humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobadil is a famous braggart, so the adjective for excessive boastful pride suits him.

clue.text: Lack of knowledge of the green

definitions.text: Lack of knowledge of the green

parts.words: Lack of knowledge of the green
parts.note: green means callow or untried, so the state of the green is a want of experience; it also suggests not knowing a golf green

explanation.surface: A golfer who doesn't know the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green means being raw and untried, without practical skill.

clue.text: Tomnoddy fell into one ?

parts.note: split as Tom noddy: a tomcat nodding off, falling into a brief doze

explanation.surface: A fool (a tomnoddy) tumbling into something.
explanation.definitionFit: A short daytime doze, the sort a nodding tomcat would take.

clue.text: They are far from mean

parts.note: mean here is the average, not stingy; what lies far from it are the outermost values

explanation.surface: Praise for generous people who are far from stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme values sit at the far ends of a range, furthest from the average.

clue.text: Pious bird of the state of Louisiana

definitions.text: Pious bird of the state of Louisiana

parts.words: Pious bird of the state of Louisiana
parts.note: heraldry shows this bird 'in her piety' feeding young on her own blood, and it is Louisiana's state bird

explanation.surface: A devout bird representing a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The large pouched waterbird is the official bird of Louisiana and a traditional emblem of piety.

clue.text: Coxcomb invites a bird for a quick visit

parts.note: to pop in is to make a quick call
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A dandy inviting a bird round for a brief call.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, showy, conceited fellow, a fop.

clue.text: Grand Prix racer heads favourites, they're beaten on the line

indicators.note: the racer heads, goes in front of, the next piece

parts.note: a racing car competes in a Grand Prix
pets are favourites, as a teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A Formula One car leads the favourites across the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugs were once hung over a washing line and beaten to remove dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Floor rugs are traditionally hung on a clothes line and thrashed to clean them.

clue.text: Unselfish type supplies a catalogue — contents not all true

indicators.note: the shortened word becomes the contents placed within the catalogue word

parts.note: a list is a catalogue of items

indicators.note: not all of the word true is used: its final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A selfless person hands over a catalogue whose contents are partly false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' drops the final letter, and 'contents' is a container signal disguised as a noun; 'supplies' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts others' welfare before their own.

clue.text: Brother keeps his upper half shut

definitions.text: Brother keeps his upper half shut

parts.words: Brother keeps his upper half shut
parts.note: a monk of a silent order keeps his trap shut, and in this down entry the upper half of the word is literally a trap

explanation.surface: A friar keeps his top half closed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks of this Cistercian order are known for keeping silence.

clue.text: Why, what's the answer? This for a start

definitions.text: Why, what's the answer? This for a start

parts.words: Why, what's the answer? This for a start
parts.note: the usual reply to a why question begins with this word, the conjunction that gives a reason

explanation.surface: A puzzled person asking why and what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply explaining a reason opens with the conjunction meaning for the reason that.

clue.text: Implement to give writer an incisive style ?

definitions.text: Implement to give writer an incisive style ?

parts.words: Implement to give writer an incisive style ?
parts.note: a small blade once used to cut quills, read as a tool that makes a writer's pen cutting

explanation.surface: A tool that might make an author's prose sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding blade originally used to sharpen quill pens.

clue.text: 'ad uneasy craving to get married

definitions.meaning: had a restless desire, felt a longing
to be hitched, spoken in the Cockney way that the clue's 'ad shows, with the opening H dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ad tells the solver to speak like a Cockney, so getting hitched loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling a restless longing is having an itch; being wed is being hitched, minus its initial letter in dialect.

clue.text: Lord Greystoke with his African family tree

definitions.text: Lord Greystoke with his African family tree

parts.words: Lord Greystoke with his African family tree
parts.note: the titled English heir raised by apes in the African jungle, whose family literally lived in the trees

explanation.surface: A peer researching his African ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs's ape-raised jungle hero is heir to the Greystoke title.

clue.text: The calling of Uncle .Tom near dissolution

indicators.note: the words are dissolved and their letters reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Uncle Tom near death hears his calling.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of naming, the act of calling things by names.

clue.text: New wine essential

definitions.meaning: something you have to do or see

explanation.definitionFit: Grape juice before fermentation; and a thing that is a necessity.

clue.text: One hit on the head — and no mistake!

definitions.text: One hit on the head — and no mistake!

parts.words: One hit on the head — and no mistake!
parts.note: a hammer strikes this squarely on its head, and hitting it on the head means getting something exactly right

explanation.surface: Someone struck on the head, emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal fastener is driven by blows to its head; hitting one squarely is the idiom for being exactly right.

clue.text: Like Wimsey's creator, they prove their metal

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: Writers like Dorothy Sayers proving their mettle.
explanation.walkthrough: Metal puns on mettle; to prove metal is to test its purity.
explanation.definitionFit: Testers analyse ores and metals to establish their composition and purity.

clue.text: Petition points to international agreement

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
a treaty is a formal agreement between nations

explanation.surface: A petition referring to an international accord.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest request or plea.
